findings.title: Translation LRU cache key ignores the site-specific fallback locale
findings.body: The cache key for memoized translations is built only from the key, the current locale and the backend object id (`k = "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`). With this PR, the resolved value of a translation now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale` (via `FallbackLocaleList`), and that setting is per-site on multisite installs and can be changed at runtime — but it is not part of the cache key, and the cache itself (`@cache` on the I18n singleton) is process-global. Consequences: (1) on a multisite cluster sharing one process, a key missing in locale X is resolved through whichever site's default locale populated the cache first — e.g. a user on a site whose default is German can be served the French fallback string cached for another site, until the 300-entry LRU happens to evict it; (2) on a single site, after an admin changes `default_locale`, fallback strings in the old language keep being served from the cache until eviction. Previously (`config.i18n.fallbacks = true`) the fallback target was the global `I18n.default_locale`, so cached entries were consistent. Include `SiteSetting.default_locale` (or the resolved fallback chain) in the cache key, or clear `I18n`'s cache when the setting changes.

findings.title: Fallback locale files are only loaded for controller requests, so fallbacks silently fail in jobs/mailers/rake
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only invoked from the `set_locale` before_filter, i.e. only for HTTP requests through ApplicationController. The translate accelerator's `translate` only ever loads yml files for `config.locale` (`load_locale(config.locale)`); it never loads the fallback locales itself. Any server-side code that translates outside a web request — Sidekiq jobs, ActionMailer views, rake tasks, console — with `I18n.locale` set to a non-English locale will walk the fallback chain (locale → site default → :en), find that no translations were ever loaded for the fallback locales, and render "translation missing: xx.yyy" instead of the site-default/English string. So the feature this PR adds silently does not work in exactly the server-side contexts that don't pass through a controller. Load the fallback locales inside the accelerator instead (e.g. have `I18n.ensure_loaded!`/`translate` load every locale in `I18n.fallbacks[locale]`), or route jobs/mailers through the same ensure_loaded! step.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList#[] does a SiteSetting read and several array allocations on every interpolated translation
findings.body: The i18n fallbacks backend calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every backend lookup, and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read plus `[locale, ...].uniq.compact` (multiple array allocations) each time. The translate accelerator only memoizes argument-free lookups — every `I18n.t` call with interpolation options (the common case in this codebase, e.g. anything with `count:` or a username) bypasses the LRU cache and pays this cost per call, in a code path that exists specifically to make translation fast. Consider memoizing the computed list keyed by (locale, default_locale) and invalidating when the setting changes.

findings.title: No tests for the new fallback semantics, which now apply to all environments
findings.body: This PR rewrites how fallbacks are computed (new `FallbackLocaleList`, new `I18n.ensure_loaded!`, per-request `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!`) and, as a side effect, enables fallbacks in every environment — previously they were only turned on via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true` in the production-like configs, so in development/test a key present in English but missing in the active locale now silently renders the English text instead of a "translation missing" message. No specs cover any of this. At minimum, add coverage that `I18n.fallbacks[:xx]` returns `[xx, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq`, that a key missing in the active locale resolves through the site default and then English, and that the fallback locale files are actually loaded (the `ensure_loaded!` path).
